mechanism: Confirmed, including the -blocksonly half, which is the part with no mitigation. Core sets fBroadcastTransactions once from SetBroadcastTransactions(GetBoolArg("-walletbroadcast", DEFAULT_WALLETBROADCAST)) (refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/wallet.cpp:3068) and reads it at three places: CommitTransaction returns BEFORE submitting to the local mempool (wallet.cpp:2341-2344, comment 'Don't submit tx to the mempool'), ShouldResend returns false (wallet.cpp:2063-2064) and ResubmitWalletTransactions returns even when forced (wallet.cpp:2109-2110). Core also SOFT-SETS -walletbroadcast=0 whenever -blocksonly=1 (wallet/init.cpp:95-97, logging 'Parameter interaction: -blocksonly=1 -> setting -walletbroadcast=0'), so a blocksonly operator never has to ask for it. Ours: -walletbroadcast is a :core-only row (src/config-options.lisp:454) and there is no fBroadcastTransactions analogue -- a do-symbols sweep of every BITCOIN-LISP* package for a bound special whose name contains BROADCAST returns nine symbols, all of them relay-timing constants and *NEXT-INITIAL-BROADCAST-TIME*, none a flag. %WALLET-SUBMIT-TX (src/wallet/wallet-spend.lisp:2466-2501) validates, calls accept-validated-tx and then, on the caller's :relay, mempool-add-unbroadcast plus broadcast-transaction-to-peers; the only caller that can pass :relay NIL is the resubmit pass, and %wallet-commit-transaction (:2517) hardcodes :relay t. APPLY-PARAMETER-INTERACTIONS (src/node/args.lisp:147-270) implements the -blocksonly interaction for -maxmempool only, with no -walletbroadcast row.
consequence: -walletbroadcast=0 is how an operator keeps a signed transaction off the wire -- the air-gapped, coinjoin and paid-submission workflows -- and the action it is meant to prevent is irreversible: once the txid is queued to a peer it links the transaction to this node's IP and cannot be recalled. Executed on regtest with -walletbroadcast=0 -blocksonly=1 in force, a wallet sendtoaddress reaches the local mempool, is added to the unbroadcast set AND lands in a relay-capable peer's tx-inv queue -- the shipped announcement queue, drained by flush-tx-announcements on a purely time-based schedule (src/networking/protocol.lisp:3125-3162: the only conditions are peer readiness, tx-relay state and the Poisson timer, no further gate). Refuter check on the warning line, and this is where the two halves differ: a directly supplied -walletbroadcast=0 IS named in the startup WARN (supplied-core-only-options returns ("walletbroadcast")), but the -blocksonly=1 operator supplied no such option, so it can never be named -- Core would have turned the wallet broadcaster off for them and we neither do it nor mention it. Refuter check on scope: the wire half is a TEST-NETWORK fact as shipped. relay-enabled-p (src/networking/peer.lisp:754-763) gates relay-transaction on *mainnet-relay-enabled*, which is NIL and has no option, start-node keyword or setter anywhere in the tree, so on mainnet a wallet transaction is accepted into the local mempool but never announced. The wallet is default-ON on the test networks and default-OFF on mainnet, so the networks where the wallet actually runs are exactly the ones where the announcement happens. Refuter check on a workaround: the `send` RPC's add_to_wallet=false / psbt=true path (%finish-transaction, src/wallet/wallet-spend.lisp:3056-3066) does return the hex or PSBT instead of committing, so a careful operator has a per-call escape hatch -- but sendtoaddress and sendmany have none, and a per-call option is not the node-wide default -walletbroadcast=0 is, nor does it silence the rebroadcast pass.
evidence: Probe build/ga11v/p-wbcast.lisp (worktree fix/ga11v-options-s2a, warm image). (1) Config: args->start-node-plist on (-regtest -walletbroadcast=0 -blocksonly=1 -wallet=w) => :PLIST (:LISTEN T :WALLET T :WALLET-NAMES ("w") :BLOCKSONLY T :NETWORK :REGTEST) -- -blocksonly reaches a keyword, -walletbroadcast reaches nothing -- :SUPPLIED-CORE-ONLY ("walletbroadcast"). (2) Exhaustive absence: the BROADCAST sweep returns only BITCOIN-LISP.NETWORKING *NEXT-INITIAL-BROADCAST-TIME* and eight +...-BROADCAST-INTERVAL+/+INV-BROADCAST-TARGET+ constants -- no fBroadcastTransactions. (3) END-TO-END: with-wallet-chain-node on regtest, the operator's line applied through BOTH apply-config-globals and apply-parameter-interactions, wallet funded and matured, one relay-capable peer attached, then rpc-sendtoaddress => (:RELAY-ENABLED-P T :TXID 35b4d107f03e9ee260b1c3a79f616fcd58e9c12ed4c713d584e1f0c544346366 :IN-LOCAL-MEMPOOL T :IN-UNBROADCAST-SET T :PEER-TX-INV-QUEUE-LENGTH 1 :PEER-QUEUE-HOLDS-THIS-TXID T :MAX-MEMPOOL-BYTES-AFTER-BLOCKSONLY 5000000). The last value is the POSITIVE CONTROL: *max-mempool-bytes* moved to 5,000,000, so apply-parameter-interactions genuinely ran and the -blocksonly soft-set machinery was live -- it simply has no -walletbroadcast row. Files: src/wallet/wallet-spend.lisp:2466-2521,2555-2588,3056-3066, src/node/args.lisp:147-168, src/node/mempool-persist.lisp:3-14, src/networking/protocol.lisp:2873-2913,3125-3186, src/networking/peer.lisp:754-763, src/node/params.lisp:81, src/config-options.lisp:454; refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/wallet.cpp:2063-2064,2109-2110,2341-2344,3068, refs/bitcoin/src/wallet/init.cpp:95-97.
fix_shape: Port fBroadcastTransactions as a per-wallet-manager (or per-node) flag rather than a call-site argument, because Core reads it at three sites and a caller-passed :relay only covers one. Promote -walletbroadcast out of define-core-only-options into a real boolean option defaulting to true, resolve it once during startup, and gate the three places Core gates: %wallet-commit-transaction must return before %wallet-submit-tx when it is false (Core stops before the LOCAL mempool, so passing :relay NIL is not equivalent -- the tx must not be accepted at all), the resubmit candidate scan must return immediately, and wallets-maybe-resend must no-op. Then add the missing row to apply-parameter-interactions next to the existing -maxmempool one: when -blocksonly is true and -walletbroadcast was not explicitly supplied, soft-set it to false and log Core's exact 'Parameter interaction: -blocksonly=1 -> setting -walletbroadcast=0' line; the soft-set must lose to an explicit -walletbroadcast=1, which is why it belongs in apply-parameter-interactions after apply-option-globals rather than in the option's own row. Test it through the shipped RPC with a relay-capable peer attached and assert the peer's tx-inv queue stays EMPTY, with the queue-is-non-empty default run kept as the positive control.
